canonical_source.behavior: When the shared grid has selected keys, ClearSelectionAsync clears the local selected-key set and then invokes SelectionChanged with the now-empty collection. The action is selection-state only and does not persist or call WordPress.

semantics: the existing Sites Clear selection action remains the single visible control; no duplicate button or parallel workflow is introduced
the shared contract clears browser-local selection first and then raises the optional empty-selection callback, matching AppDataGrid ClearSelectionCoreAsync ordering
the control renders only while at least one authoritative Sites row is selected
the real consumer clears only the selected IDs already loaded from the active tenant-scoped Sites collection
clear selection issues no DELETE, POST, PUT, PATCH, WordPress, queue, cache, billing, or secret operation
the owning Sites mutation busy state disables the control to avoid racing a destructive operation

security.tenant_context: auth + tenant.context on the owning Sites workspace
security.foreign_tenant_access: 404 fail closed on the authoritative Sites API before foreign rows can reach the control

proofs: exact canonical operation marker and source-operation key
existing Sites clear-selection UI reused rather than duplicated
no mutation request while clearing selected rows
foreign tenant authoritative Sites API returns 404

terminality.basis: Laravel now binds the exact AppDataGrid ClearSelectionAsync contract to the already-existing tenant-scoped Sites clear-selection action through one reusable shared control. Focused frontend and PHP tests prove source ordering, no mutation, canonical identity, authoritative API tenancy, and foreign-tenant fail-closed behavior.
